results.title: Host API answers a health probe
results.observed: GET /health → 200 {"ok":true,"product":"SECH_LIMS by Nickland","lanReady":true}

results.title: System and connectivity detail is refused to an unauthenticated caller
results.observed: GET /system/about → 401, GET /system/connectivity → 401 (commonRoutes applies requireAuth to the whole router)

results.title: Credentials and records can travel over an encrypted channel
results.observed: This run is on loopback, where traffic never leaves the machine. The Host serves HTTPS when SECH_LIMS_TLS_CERT and SECH_LIMS_TLS_KEY are set, and prints an explicit warning at startup if it is bound to a network address without them (server/index.ts). TLS on the target deployment is verified by IQ-W7.

results.observed: setupComplete=false adminExists=false

results.title: First administrator can be established
results.observed: POST /setup/initialize → 201 {"ok":true}

results.title: Setup cannot be re-run to create a second unaudited administrator
results.observed: Second POST /setup/initialize → 400 {"error":"Initial setup has already been completed."}

results.title: System reports setup as complete once initialised
results.observed: setupComplete=true adminExists=true

results.title: Invalid credentials are refused
results.observed: → 401 {"error":"Invalid username or password"}

results.title: Valid credentials are accepted and issue a session token
results.observed: → 200, token length 64

results.title: Login response never returns the stored password hash
results.observed: No bcrypt material present in the authentication response.

results.title: Session tokens are not stored in reusable form
results.observed: auth_sessions columns are [id, user_id, token_hash, device_id, ip_address, expires_at, last_seen_at, created_at, revoked_at] — the token column is gone, and what remains is a 64-character digest that is not the bearer token. Read access to the database no longer yields a working session.

results.title: Protected endpoint refuses an unauthenticated caller
results.observed: GET /users without a token → 401

results.title: Protected endpoint refuses a forged token
results.observed: GET /users with a fabricated token → 401

results.title: Repeated failed sign-in attempts lock the account
results.observed: Locked after 5 consecutive failures; the correct password was then refused too (429), so the lock is not bypassed by finally guessing right.

results.title: The lockout is recorded in the audit trail
results.observed: 1 account_locked entries recorded.

results.title: A trivial password is refused when an account is created
results.observed: The password "password" → 400 "Use at least 12 characters. A short phrase you will remember is stronger than a short word with symbols in it."

results.title: Minimum password length is enforced
results.observed: A 3-character password → 400 {"error":"Use at least 12 characters. A short phrase you will remember is stronger than a short word with symbols in it."}

results.title: Signing out revokes the session token immediately
results.observed: before logout → 200, after logout → 401

results.title: A session expires after a period of inactivity
results.observed: Session was live before ageing (200); after 35 minutes of simulated inactivity it was refused (401).

results.observed: action=create entity=users actor=1 at=2026-08-10 11:18:21 ip=127.0.0.1

results.title: Successful and failed sign-ins are recorded in the audit trail
results.observed: 5 login_success and 6 login_failed entries, each carrying username, IP and time — so an access review can reconstruct who signed in and what was attempted.

results.title: Audit timestamps state their time zone
results.observed: recorded_at is "2026-08-10T11:18:21.267Z" — ISO-8601 with an explicit zone, so the instant an entry describes can be proved from the record itself rather than assumed.

results.title: The application exposes no route that edits or deletes audit entries
results.observed: PUT → 404, DELETE → 404 (no such routes are defined)

results.title: Tampering with the audit trail is detectable
results.observed: Chain verification over 18 entries → ok=true, altered=[], broken=[]. Detection of a rewritten or deleted entry is proven by unit test (tests/auditChain.test.ts), which edits the database behind the application and confirms the verifier reports it.

results.title: The routine data-integrity scan verifies the audit chain
results.observed: Scan → 200, issuesFound=0, status=passed

results.title: A regulated action can be electronically signed
results.observed: POST /signatures → 201 {"id":1,"purpose":"oq_validation_approval","meaning":"Reviewed and approved for operational qualification.","signerName":"OQ Validation Administrator","signedAt":"2026-08-10T11:18:22.369Z"}

results.title: The signature records the signer, the instant and the meaning
results.observed: signer=OQ Validation Administrator at=2026-08-10 11:18:22 meaning="Reviewed and approved for operational qualification."

results.title: The signature is bound to the record it signs
results.observed: Signature is retrieved by (module=personnel, type=staff, id=1).

results.title: Signing is refused without an authenticated identity
results.observed: An unauthenticated POST /signatures is refused.

results.title: Signing requires re-entry of the signer's password
results.observed: Signing with a valid session but no password → 400; with the wrong password → 401. Holding an unattended session is no longer enough to sign in somebody else's name.

results.title: A record edited after signing is flagged against its signature
results.observed: At signing: content_hash=cb0258700c93458d…, contentChanged=false. After the record was edited: contentChanged=true. A signature can therefore show whether the record still says what it said when it was approved.

results.title: The signature points at its own audit entry
results.observed: audit_log_id=24. The id comes back from the insert that wrote it, rather than being guessed at as "the newest row in the table", so concurrent activity cannot attach the wrong entry to a signature.

results.title: A refused signing attempt is recorded
results.observed: 1 e_sign_refused entries from the wrong-password attempt above.

results.title: A data-integrity scan can be run and records its findings
results.observed: → 200 {"ok":true,"id":2,"checkNumber":"DIC-2026-0002","recordsChecked":25,"issuesFound":0,"status":"passed","findings":"No issues detected by basic scan."}

results.observed: → 201 {"fileName":"sech-lims-backup-2026-08-10T11-18-22-408Z.zip","manifest":{"product":"SECH_LIMS by Nickland","createdAt":"2026-08-10T11:18:22.409Z","includes":["SQLite database","uploads","evidence","con

results.title: Backups are registered and listable for review
results.observed: → 200, 1 package(s) registered

results.title: Each backup carries a checksum so its integrity can be proven
results.observed: SHA-256 recorded with the package: 0d59db316a94c538…. It is checked again before any restore, and a mismatch stops the restore rather than overwriting live data (verified in PQ-4.x and tests/backupIntegrity.test.ts).

results.title: Backup download refuses a path-traversal file name
results.observed: GET /backup/download/../../package.json → 400

results.title: Restore is preceded by an automatic safety snapshot
results.observed: The restore route writes a pre-restore-*.zip of current state before replacing the database, uploads, evidence and config, and aborts the restore if that snapshot cannot be written (server/routes/common.ts).

results.title: Backups are encrypted at rest
results.observed: Backup packages remain unencrypted ZIPs holding the whole database, uploads and evidence. Their integrity can now be proven (OQ-7.4) but their confidentiality cannot: an off-site copy still carries the complete quality record in the clear. Open as VF-07; the interim control is to keep off-site copying disabled or pointed at an encrypted volume.

results.title: The database itself is encrypted at rest
results.observed: sech_lims.sqlite is a plain unencrypted SQLite file. Anyone with file-level access to the host — or to a stolen laptop — reads every record without authenticating to the application.

results.title: Malformed JSON is rejected without crashing the host
results.observed: Truncated JSON body → 500

results.title: Error responses do not disclose internal implementation detail
results.observed: Error body was {"error":"Unexpected end of JSON input"}

results.title: SQL metacharacters in credentials do not bypass authentication
results.observed: Injection attempt in username/password → 401

results.title: The host remains available after malformed and hostile input
results.observed: GET /health → 200

results.title: Standard security response headers are set
results.observed: x-content-type-options, x-frame-options, content-security-policy, referrer-policy — CSP is "default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; style-src 's…". Strict-Transport-Security is sent only when the Host is serving TLS, which is correct: asserting HSTS over plain HTTP is meaningless.

results.title: Cross-origin access is restricted to known clients
results.observed: An arbitrary origin got Access-Control-Allow-Origin: (none — refused); the Host's own origin got http://127.0.0.1:4477. The allow-list covers loopback, the configured public URL, the Host's LAN addresses and SECH_LIMS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS.

results.title: An automated regression test suite is maintained
results.observed: Runner: vitest; "npm test" runs 4 suites (auditChain.test.ts, backupIntegrity.test.ts, credentials.test.ts, permissionResolver.test.ts) covering the credential policy, the audit hash chain, backup integrity and the permission resolver.

results.title: The release carries a controlled version identifier
results.observed: Version 1.0.0; /system/about reports release "1.0.0 (214be8c)" (provenance: source). CI stamps the commit into the build, so a deployed installation can be tied back to the source it came from.

results.title: Continuous integration runs the verification checks before a build
results.observed: verify.yml runs typecheck, unit tests, the structure check, the build, both qualification suites and every supplier check script; the packaging workflows (build-android-apk.yml, build-windows-installer.yml) all declare "needs: verify", so nothing is packaged from a build that failed its own checks.

results.title: The distributed installer is signed
results.observed: electron-builder is configured with no code-signing certificate ("publish": null, unsigned NSIS output). Windows SmartScreen warns on install and the laboratory cannot prove the installer it runs is the one the supplier built.

results.title: Third-party components are free of known vulnerabilities
results.observed: The shipped software now carries a single advisory: xlsx (prototype pollution and ReDoS), for which no fixed release exists on npm — SheetJS publishes fixes only from its own registry, so replacing or re-sourcing it is a supply-chain decision for the system owner. multer, adm-zip and react-router were patched. The remaining 30 advisories are all in build tooling (electron-builder, @capacitor/cli, @vercel/node) and none of it reaches a running installation. CI now blocks on criticals in shipped code and reports the full tree every run.

results.title: A dependency review runs on every build
results.observed: verify.yml runs "npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=critical" as a gate and a full-tree audit for information, so a new advisory in shipped code stops a release rather than waiting to be noticed.
